Research Objective: Test infrastructure resilience by randomly terminating virtual machine instances
Key Limitations: No security fault injection; no adaptive mitigation; relies on human remediation

Approach / Reference: Chaos as a Software Product Line (Camacho et al., SP&E 2022)
Research Objective: Configurable chaos experimentation across hybrid cloud environments
Threat / Failure Scenarios: Network delay, packet loss, pod crash, disk exhaustion
Key Metrics: Experiment execution time, failure detection rate
Key Limitations: Static scripted execution; no autonomous closed-loop mitigation engine
Key Difference from SecChaos-RL: SecChaos-RL provides automated closed-loop policy learning that actively remediates security chaos in real time.

Research Objective: Controlled evaluation of microservice resiliency patterns (retries, circuit breakers)
System Architecture: Kubernetes operator with CRDs & test harness
Action Space: Configuration of retry counts, timeouts, breakers
Key Metrics: Tail latency (p95/p99), checkout success rate, throughput
Key Limitations: Focuses on pre-configured resilience patterns for performance/availability; does not address security threats or autonomous policy adaptation
Key Difference from SecChaos-RL: SecChaos-RL targets security chaos with threat-aware representation learning to balance security, availability, and MTTR.

Approach / Reference: Self-Healing Frameworks Survey (Schneider et al., SP&E 2015)
Research Objective: Survey and taxonomy of multi-tier self-healing software frameworks
System Architecture: Closed MAPE-K control loop (Monitor, Analyze, Plan, Execute)
Action Space: Service restart, component replication, traffic rerouting
Decision Mechanism: Rule-based, heuristic, and early ML control loops
Threat / Failure Scenarios: Hardware faults, memory leaks, crash failures
Practical Deployment Evidence: Survey of diverse academic and industrial prototypes
Key Limitations: Predates modern cloud-native microservices; lacks security chaos models and deep reinforcement learning
Key Difference from SecChaos-RL: SecChaos-RL operationalizes the MAPE-K loop using deep RL with self-attention and threat gating under continuous security chaos.

Research Objective: Gym environment for training autonomous cyber defense agents in network security
System Architecture: Gym simulation / emulation environment for Red vs Blue agents
State Representation: Host IP, open ports, compromised credentials, network topology
Action Space: Subnet scanning, host isolation, service restore, decoys
Threat / Failure Scenarios: Multi-stage cyber attack kill-chain (scanning, privilege escalation, lateral movement)
Baselines: Sleep agent, random agent, static heuristic agent
Key Limitations: Static network topology and fixed attack graphs; ignores microservice dependency cascades, runtime availability, and chaos injection
Key Difference from SecChaos-RL: SecChaos-RL models dynamic security chaos in microservice DAGs with operational service availability and resource overhead trade-offs.

Research Objective: Review and framework for autonomous penetration testing using deep RL
Action Space: Exploit execution, credential dumping, lateral movement
Key Metrics: Attack success rate, steps to target host
Key Limitations: Offensive focus only; no defensive self-healing, service availability monitoring, or resilience trade-offs
Key Difference from SecChaos-RL: SecChaos-RL is an autonomous defender framework balancing security hardening with live microservice availability.

Research Objective: Automate threat discovery in design and detect security flaws via SCE in DevSecOps
System Architecture: LLM-assisted threat modeling with manual SCE injection scripts
State Representation: Natural language threat models & CI/CD pipeline state
Threat / Failure Scenarios: Missing authentication, exposed endpoints, secret leakage
Experimental Environment: Retail company CI/CD pipeline case study
Key Metrics: Vulnerability detection rate, time to identify flaw
Practical Deployment Evidence: Case study in commercial retail environment
Key Limitations: Static design-time and build-time analysis; lacks runtime self-healing and continuous closed-loop policy adaptation
Key Difference from SecChaos-RL: SecChaos-RL executes continuous runtime mitigation using an adaptive RL policy trained directly on chaos-induced operational telemetry.

Research Objective: Autonomous, threat-aware resilience engineering balancing security, availability, and recovery under security chaos
System Architecture: Closed-loop software resilience architecture (ChaosEngine, DependencyTopology, ThreatAwareOrchestrator, MitigationExecutor, BenchmarkHarness)
State Representation: 16-dimensional telemetry vector (risks, threat severity, vulnerability, resource metrics, availability, MTTR)
Action Space: 9 mitigation actions with asynchronous delays and resource costs
Decision Mechanism: PPO with Multi-Head Self-Attention, threat-aware gating, auxiliary risk prediction, and adaptive temperature exploration
Threat / Failure Scenarios: 8 security fault categories (TLS, dependencies, secrets, RBAC, MFA, patches, privileges, API) with cascading DAG propagation
Experimental Environment: Standardized Gymnasium microservice simulation environment with multi-seed benchmarking
Baselines: No-Mitigation, Static Rule-Based, Threshold-Based, DQN, A2C, standard PPO
Key Metrics: Risk reduction, Service availability, MTTR, Attack success rate, Resilience score, Decision latency, False mitigation rate
Practical Deployment Evidence: Open, modular software framework with standardized interfaces ready for Kubernetes integration
Key Limitations: Simulation environment requires real-world Kubernetes validation as future work
Key Difference from SecChaos-RL: Integrates dynamic security chaos with a safety-aware, multi-objective RL agent that actively balances security isolation with microservice availability.
